Empty — nobody in frame, nothing held, nothing staged, nothing tidied for the photograph. One age of building, one decade of decoration, one standard of upkeep. The staircase rises straight up along the LEFT-hand wall, a flight of thirteen light-grey carpeted steps to the landing, with a light-oak handrail on plain white square spindles on its open right-hand side and a white newel post with an oak cap at the bottom. On the right-hand wall a row of coat hooks with a navy work jacket and a camel coat, a slim shoe rack below with a pair of tan leather work boots and white trainers, a small round mirror and a framed family photo too small to read.
